title: Alignment daybook: crosswalk notes Product + Eng + Applied ML
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Quick capture from 06-07 cross-functional alignment huddle (Product + Eng + Applied ML). Owner notes for follow-ups and rough plan we can iterate on. Keep this as a single-source-of-truth daybook for the next sprint boundary.

Attendees (by role):
- Product: Nora Chen (product lead)
- Eng: Ravi Patel (serving runtime), Marcus Lee (platform infra)
- Applied ML: Lina Gómez (inference optimizations)
- Note taker / owner: Akshay Mehta

Meeting objectives (explicit):
1) Reconcile Q3 milestone for "low-latency multi-tenant rollout" across teams.
2) Surface research spikes needed to support quantized 8-bit variants on our Dedicated fleet.
3) Agree on acceptance criteria and monitoring hooks for canary rollout.

Quick outcome summary (headline):
- High-level milestone kept: target GA-ish date remains Aug 19 (internal).
- Scope trimmed: initial rollout will support top-3 customer models and two inference modes (streaming + non-streaming).
- Actionable risks surfaced: eval gap for hallucination under quantization; infra autoscaler latency under heavy prefix caching.

Notes / decisions (explicit):
- Decision 1: Ship canary to Dedicated pool only for first pass (no hosted API traffic). Rationale: containment + easier rollback.
- Decision 2: Enable prefix cache warmup in canary but keep KV-store eviction at default; will instrument in observability first.
- Decision 3: Accept temporary 3-5% throughput regression for 8-bit quantized path if latency SLOs hold. Re-evaluate after research spike.

Open questions (prioritized):
- Q1: How do we measure "quality delta" for quantized models in a repeatable way? Lina proposes a 3-metric composite (BLEU-like where applicable, token-based perplexity, and prompt-based hallucination score). Action: Lina to draft the evaluation harness.
- Q2: Can platform autoscaler respond quickly enough to prefix-warmup spikes? Marcus to run a synthetic spike test and report P95 reaction time.
- Q3: Do we need a soft-limit for canary concurrency to avoid noisy neighbor effects? Ravi/Marcus to propose configuration in next 48h.

Back-of-envelope tradeoffs noted (for context):
- Latency vs cost: 8-bit quantized path reduces GPU memory pressure allowing higher batch sizes -> cost down ~12-20% in optimistic case; but KV cache and prefetching may increase per-request latency variance.
- Reliability vs rollout speed: Dedicated-only canary lowers blast radius but delays host-level learnings (some hosted-specific infra differences). Plan: follow Dedicated canary with small hosted beta within 2 weeks if canary stable.

Concrete action items (owner - due)
- Lina: Draft evaluation harness repo & sample prompt set (baseline vs quantized) and initial hallucination metric proposal - due 2026-06-14.
- Marcus: Run autoscaler synthetic spike (prefix warmup profile) and capture P50/P95/P99 scaling latency; include infra config suggestions - due 2026-06-11.
- Ravi: Prototype conservative canary runtime config (concurrency cap, KV eviction policy, fallback to float model) and short runbook for rollback - due 2026-06-11.
- Nora: Update product kickoff doc to reflect narrowed scope and customer prioritization (top-3 models list) - due 2026-06-09.
- Akshay (me): Create canary dashboard skeleton in Console (latency, token-cost, model-quality regression heatmap) and invite reviewers - due 2026-06-12.

Acceptance criteria draft for canary (workable checklist):
- Functional: end-to-end inference path for selected models runs without errors at baseline traffic profile.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency <= current SLO + 15% for quantized path during canary window.
- Quality: automated eval harness shows <2% net increase in hallucination score vs baseline (subject to Lina's metric).
- Observability: dashboard shows token-level cost, per-request trace id, and a daily regression digest.

Rollback criteria (if any of the following trigger):
- Quality breach: automated eval shows >5% regression in hallucination metric for two consecutive daily runs.
- Latency breach: sustained P95 > current SLO + 30% for >30 minutes.
- Stability: >1% error rate at request level for 1 hour.

Notes on experiment & instrumentation (technical details):
- Eval harness will run on a shadowed copy of customer prompts (anonymized) and use deterministic seeds where possible. Lina will keep dataset size small for quick daily runs (~2k prompts).
- Add a per-request header flag to mark canary traffic so metrics pipeline can isolate metrics (trace + sample of token stream).
- Add a regression alert that runs nightly comparing canary baseline to float baseline. Integrate with PagerDuty only for severity breaches.

Follow-ups scheduled:
- Short standup sync (15m) next Tue 06-09 to triage early infra results (Marcus + Ravi + Akshay).
- Deep evaluation sync (30m) 06-14 after Lina's harness deliverable.

Risks & mitigations (short list):
- Research risk: quantization produces subtle quality regressions in long-context prompts. Mitigation: expand prompt set during harness and enable quick fallback to float model with traffic split.
- Ops risk: autoscaler thrash under prefix-warmup. Mitigation: conservative concurrency caps and short-lived pre-warm warmers during canary.

Random scribbles / ideas to revisit later:
- Explore fast-drop-in fallback where we route tokens to float model only when hallucination confidence low (experimental classifier).
- Consider a "safety-sampling" periodic test that runs small transforms of customer prompts to detect hallucination drift automatically.

Immediate next steps (today / next 48h):
- Akshay: create this doc in Drive and ping owners in Slack (done).
- Marcus/Ravi: confirm time for synthetic spike test and post results into linked Jira.
- Lina: start skeleton of eval harness and list minimal metrics.

Appendix: sample Slack nudges / reminders (copy-paste)
- "@Lina hi — can you drop the evaluation harness repo link here when ready? Want to sync 06-14. Thx."
- "@Marcus @Ravi — please post the autoscaler test results to RDW-4871 and tag 'infra-urgent' if P95 > 60s."

File note: keep this as living doc; update with links to PRs, dashboards, and confluence page as they appear.
